title: Operationalizing safety metrics and auto-safe-shutoff for model swaps
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Create a production-ready, testable playbook and automation layer that uses composite safety signals to automatically 'safe-shutoff' (circuit-break) model swaps and rollouts. This ticket covers: 1) defining a small set of orthogonal safety signals that meaningfully predict user-visible regressions during canary/A-B/gradual model swaps (latency tail percentiles, token-level divergence, hallucination score regressions from eval sets, error-rate increase on critical routes, and KV cache collision metrics), 2) designing a deterministic scoring function and hysteresis rules that map signal combinations to actions (pause traffic, step down to prior model variant, or trigger immediate rollback), 3) implementing automation in the rollout controller to apply the actions with safe gating and audit trail, 4) authoring an operational runbook for SREs and on-call engaged during swaps, and 5) providing a synthetic failure harness and acceptance tests for the automation.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Safety signal list and scoring function documented and reviewed by SRE/Research/PM.
- Rollout controller support for 'safe-shutoff' with at least these actions: PAUSE (freeze traffic), SCALE-DOWN (reduce traffic to golden variant), ROLLBACK (automated full revert), and ALERT (paged and Slack channels), including annotation of reason and metrics snapshot.
- Hysteresis implemented so transient spikes do not cause flip-flop; configuration per-customer is supported.
- Runbook published in Confluence and linked from Console's rollout UI.
- End-to-end tests that inject synthetic anomalies (latency spike, KV cache corruption, synthetic hallucination regression via eval stub) and assert the controller triggers the expected action.
- Security review completed for automation execution permissions and audit logs.

Non-goals: full ML-driven anomaly detection (this ticket standardizes deterministic rules and infra to plug ML detectors later). Deep UX changes to Console rollout flows (only links and annotations are required here).
comments: 2026-02-16 - Initial scoping sync: agreed on candidate safety signals and to prioritize low-latency observable metrics for v0. Assigned Liam to draft scoring matrix.
2026-02-22 - Engineering review: kernel/serving team noted we must include KV cache collision rate and per-shard saturation metrics; updated acceptance criteria.
2026-02-28 - SRE review: requested explicit hysteresis window (configurable) and minimum sample size before scoring; added to requirements.
2026-03-03 - Security kickoff: identified KMS access for audit signing and a short list of IAM roles the automation will assume; draft sent to security@redwood.com.

2026-03-07 - Prototype test: synthetic latency spike injected into canary group in staging; controller PAUSE action executed and a rollback did not occur due to hysteresis — behaviour matches expectation. Need longer-run tests for steady-state noise tolerance.
2026-03-10 - PM feedback: link runbook to Console route and add clear escalation steps for product-support to follow when automation fires; added subtask to documentation.
2026-03-10 - Next: finalize scoring thresholds and land controller PR, then run full synthetic-failure suite and a cross-team runbook dry-run with SRE/PM/Designers.
test_plan: E2E synthetic failure harness: 1) latency tail injection (p99+p999), 2) token-divergence using golden prompts, 3) simulated KV cache collision by duplicating keys in staging shard, 4) route-specific error-rate increase via fault-injection. Each scenario asserts controller action and checks audit entries.
postmortem_followups: Create a searchable 'swap-failure' artifact repository for failed rollouts (logs, snapshots, timeline).
Add per-customer alert templates and customer impact classification to Console when safe-shutoff fires.
Build a daily synthesis dashboard of near-miss events (scoring function crossed threshold but hysteresis avoided action) for tuning.
Schedule cross-team tabletop (SRE/Research/PM/Design) after two staged rollouts to validate runbook ergonomics.
notes_for_release: Config defaults: conservative thresholds; hysteresis window 5 minutes; minimum 100 requests/sample for route-level signals. Ops must opt-in per-customer for auto-rollback on Dedicated until 90-day maturity.
